messages:
Sasha: ran a perfetto + nsys sweep on the nightly running model. seeing long stalls during first token dispatch — looks like compilation + kernel selection piled up. attaching trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (private)
Anna: thanks — can you paste the nsys command and the time window you used?
Sasha: yep:
```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/run.nsys \
  --capture-range=cpu:tid:1-5000 ./run_inference.sh --model resnet-like
```
window: 00:00:12.500 - 00:00:14.800 (first 2 tokens after prompt)
Mike: interesting — I see two spikes in the kernel timeline separated by ~120ms. that smells like Triton/XLA-like compile time + kernel cache miss.
Jules: what's the kernel cache hit rate? any KV cache interactions that could block?
Sasha: grep from logs:
```text
[2026-03-10T12:00:12.678Z] KernelCache MISS key=conv_fwd_bs1_seq128_k=sm80
[2026-03-10T12:00:12.800Z] TritonCompile  exec_time=0.18s  kernels=3
[2026-03-10T12:00:12.980Z] KernelCache STORE key=conv_fwd_bs1_seq128_k=sm80
```
Anna: so ~180ms compile for that kernel set. plus user code orchestration -> total warmup ~240-300ms per operator?
Mike: aggregate warmup across the small MLP/attention blocks adds up — our perfetto flame shows ~1.1s spent in compile/warmup for the first attention block sequence.
Sasha: also saw KV cache behavior: when the request included a long prefix, the runtime did KV cache lookups synchronously before scheduling the kernel, adding ~30-50ms.
Jules: is KV lookup syncronous on CPU path? could we prefetch or make it async?
Anna: we have an in-flight async prefetch change in the batching heuristics PR — but it currently only triggers on >2 active requests. could tweak to prefetch for first token if seq_len>64.
Mike: quick repro idea: run nsys with environment VAR to force kernel-cache disabled: KERNEL_CACHE=0 and compare. would isolate compile time vs kernel launch stalls.
Sasha: did that — disable shows compile spikes disappear but kernel overall runtime increases (unquantized kernels) so perf tradeoff. results: 
- with cache: first request latency 1.35s, steady-state 0.12s
- without cache: first request 0.20s, steady-state 0.18s
(note: numbers approximate)
Jules: wait those numbers invert expectations — why first request faster when cache disabled?
Sasha: because our cache storage step does synchronous serialization to disk in that codepath — the STORE call blocks the thread for ~1s in our config. bug? :bug: 
Anna: aha — that explains it. we should make STORE async / write-behind. Also lease the kernel cache write to background thread.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: nightly/regression-server showed +12% p99 on model/resnet-like on 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC (linked traces: nsys abc123).
Mike: propose plan:
1) land async store for kernel cache (write-behind)
2) change prefetch heuristics to prefetch on long prefixes for first-token paths
3) add an opt-in env KERNEL_STORE_SYNC=0 default for Dedicated to mitigate immediately
4) add unit trace in CI to catch blocking STOREs
Sasha: I'll open a small PR for async store. will also attach flame screenshots.
Anna: also let's add a perfetto timeline annotation from runtime that marks "kv-lookup" and "kernel-compile" boundaries — will make it easier to eyeball.
Jules: for the CI trace, can we add nsys perf counters (eg sm_efficiency, achieved_occupancy) to ensure compile path not hiding bad kernels?
Mike: yes add `--sample-counters=cuda` and postprocess via `nsys stats` in the test harness.
Sasha: PR 4512 opened: https://git.redwood/r/4512 — UNTESTED, draft. includes async writer and KERNEL_STORE_SYNC env. pls review when possible.
Anna: assigned to me for review. quick +1 on the design, but run the nightly with it toggled to verify no regressions.
perf-bot: scheduled nightly job with KERNEL_STORE_SYNC=0 for model/resnet-like tomorrow 02:00 UTC.
ci-bot: note — added new test `trace-compile-kv` to perf-suite, will run on linux-gpu.
Sasha: thanks all. will post follow-up with updated perfetto link after next run. :thumbsup:
